chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Saeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about a man who bequeathed for a Hajj, so his executor made it regarding a person (freeing a slave). He said: 'The executor bears the cost, and he makes it regarding a Hajj just as he had been bequeathed.'
So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then the sin of it is only upon those who alter it.
Indeed Allah, Blessed and High is, says:

key_terms.حَجَّةٍ: A specific Hajj pilgrimage, often implying a bequest for one Hajj
key_terms.نَسَمَةٍ: A person (specifically for freeing a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an executor changes a bequest for Hajj to freeing a slave?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the executor is held personally liable for converting a Hajj bequest to manumission, ensuring the original intent is preserved by bearing the difference in cost. This interpretation relies on the principle that altering a bequest without valid cause incurs the spiritual penalty described in Surah al-Baqarah, emphasizing the sanctity of the testator's specific wishes. The hadith underscores the executor's fiduciary duty to act as a faithful agent of the deceased's religious obligations.
